about.heading: Not a watch party. A bracket.
paragraphs: Open Bracket is a two-day outdoor games event on Governors Island. You don't just watch creators play. You can play too, and if you do well, you play with them.
Day 1 is open qualifiers. Anyone 18 or older with a competitor ticket can enter. You get one heat of four short games, and the top three players in each heat go through. That makes 18 qualifiers.

Day 2 is the finals. The 18 qualifiers are drafted onto six teams, each captained by an invited creator. Teams play in front of a live crowd on the Parade Ground, and the whole day streams on Twitch and YouTube.

schedule.heading: Order of play
schedule.note: Times show in your time zone, with Eastern Time (the island's zone) alongside. Use the switch to flip between them. Competitors pick their heat when they register and check in at least 30 minutes before it, or the spot goes to the standby line. There is no lunch break on Day 1. Each competitor plays one heat, and the food trucks on Colonels Row are open all day.

days.label: Day 01
days.title: Open Qualifiers
days.summary: Six heats of 50 players. Each heat plays four games for points. Top three in each heat advance to the finals.

sessions.title: Check-in opens
sessions.detail: Pick up your wristband at the check-in tent on the Parade Ground. It is a 5 minute walk from both ferry landings. Check-in stays open until {{t:2026-10-17T14:30:00-04:00}}.

sessions.title: Heat 1
sessions.detail: Crate Stack, Musical Chairs, Shuttle Relay, Simon Says. Coming from Brooklyn? The first Pier 6 boat lands after Heat 1 check-in closes, so take the Manhattan ferry for this heat.

sessions.title: Heat 2
sessions.detail: Sack Sprint, Balloon Toss, Shuttle Relay, Lag Spike.

sessions.title: Heat 3
sessions.detail: Crate Stack, Musical Chairs, Sack Sprint, Simon Says.

sessions.title: Heat 4
sessions.detail: Balloon Toss, Shuttle Relay, Lag Spike, Simon Says.

sessions.title: Heat 5
sessions.detail: Crate Stack, Sack Sprint, Musical Chairs, Lag Spike.

sessions.title: Heat 6
sessions.detail: Balloon Toss, Crate Stack, Shuttle Relay, Simon Says.

sessions.title: Bracket reveal
sessions.detail: The 18 qualifiers are called up on the main stage and the Day 2 bracket goes up. Leaves time for the {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}} last ferry.

days.label: Day 02
days.title: Finals
days.summary: 18 qualifiers drafted onto six teams, each captained by an invited creator. Points round, semifinals, grand final.

sessions.title: Gates and check-in
sessions.detail: Qualifiers check in at the green tent by {{t:2026-10-18T10:15:00-04:00}}. Spectators go straight to the Parade Ground.

sessions.title: Team draft
sessions.detail: Creators pick their three qualifiers live on stage. The stream starts here.

sessions.title: Finals round 1
sessions.detail: All six teams play three games for points. Top four teams go through.

sessions.title: Creators exhibition match
sessions.detail: The six creators play Musical Chairs and Simon Says against each other. No points, just bragging rights.

sessions.title: Semifinals
sessions.detail: Four teams, two games each. Top two teams go through.

sessions.title: Grand final
sessions.detail: Two teams play Chat Decides. The route is voted on live by the crowd and stream chat.

sessions.title: Closing ceremony
sessions.detail: Trophy for the winning team, awards for top qualifier and best crate tower, and a thank you to everyone who played.

sessions.title: Ferry call
sessions.detail: Head to your landing. Last ferries leave at {{t:2026-10-18T18:00:00-04:00}}, but lines get long after the ceremony.

games.heading: The games
games.intro: Eight games. Each one takes a few minutes, needs no practice, and is easy to follow from the crowd or the stream.

items.name: Crate Stack
items.desc: Stack plastic crates as high as you can. The tower has to stand for five seconds to count.

items.name: Musical Chairs
items.format: Groups of 12 / until one is left
items.desc: The classic, played at full size on the grass with a DJ who knows when to stop.

items.name: Shuttle Relay
items.desc: Four legs, one baton, cones at each end. Drop the baton and you restart your leg.

items.name: Simon Says
items.desc: One host, 50 players, one mic. Move without "Simon says" and you are out.

items.name: Sack Sprint
items.desc: Step into a sack and jump to the finish line. Falling is allowed. Crawling is not.

items.name: Balloon Toss
items.desc: Toss a water balloon to your partner and step back after every catch. You will probably get wet.

items.name: Lag Spike
items.desc: A race where the host can call "lag" at any time, and everyone must move in slow motion until it clears.

items.name: Chat Decides
items.desc: An obstacle course where the crowd and stream chat vote on which path you take at each fork.

creators.heading: Creator lineup
creators.intro: Six invited creators play on Day 2. Each one captains a team of three qualifiers. All names below are fictional.

items.name: Rosa Asante
items.bio: Holds records in three retro platformers and streams practice runs at 6 AM.

items.name: Theo Lindqvist
items.bio: Tries a new sport every week and posts every failed attempt.

items.name: Kwame Mori
items.bio: Hosts a nightly party game stream where chat sets the house rules.

items.name: June Marchetti
items.bio: Posts one trick shot a day and shows all the misses before it.

items.name: Luis Park

items.name: Hana Ferreira
items.bio: Variety streamer known for co-op chaos and skipping every tutorial.

creators.more: Creators play Day 2 only. Meet-and-greet line opens at the merch tent during the Day 2 lunch break.

logistics.heading: Getting there
logistics.intro: Governors Island has no cars and no bridge. The only way on or off is by ferry, from Lower Manhattan or Brooklyn. Ferries are free for everyone before {{t:2026-10-17T11:00:00-04:00}} on Saturdays and Sundays. After that, buy a round-trip ticket from the ferry operator. Fares and timetables are on govisland.com.

routes.landing: Battery Maritime Building, 10 South St. Arrives at Soissons Landing.
routes.subway: 1 to South Ferry, R/W to Whitehall St, or 4/5 to Bowling Green. About a 5 minute walk.
routes.ferry: Runs daily. Every 15 minutes on weekends from {{t:2026-10-17T10:00:00-04:00}} to {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}}, every 30 minutes before that. About 7 minutes across.

routes.landing: Pier 6, Brooklyn Bridge Park, at the end of Atlantic Ave. Arrives at Yankee Pier.
routes.subway: 2/3/4/5 to Borough Hall or R to Court St, then about 15 minutes on foot.
routes.ferry: Weekends and holidays only, through November 1. Less frequent than Manhattan, so check the timetable. About 10 minutes across.

logistics.lastFerryWarning: The island closes at {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}} in the fall. Last ferries back leave at {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}} to Manhattan and to Brooklyn. If you miss them, there is no other way off the island.

cards.title: Check-in on arrival
cards.body: From either landing, follow the Open Bracket signs to the check-in tent on the Parade Ground, about 5 minutes on foot. Show the QR code from your confirmation email to get your wristband. Competitors need to check in at least 30 minutes before their heat, or the spot goes to the standby line. Spectators get a wristband at the same tent.

cards.title: What to bring
cards.body: Shoes you can run in. A change of socks and a spare shirt for Balloon Toss. Sunscreen and a hat. A warm layer, because October on the water is cold, especially on the ferry home. An empty water bottle to refill. A charged phone with your QR code.

cards.title: Water and shade
cards.body: Free water refill stations at every game field and at the main stage. Bring a refillable bottle. Shade tents and seating along Colonels Row. The medical tent is next to check-in.

cards.title: Bag policy
cards.body: Clear bags only, up to 12 x 6 x 12 in, or a one-gallon clear plastic bag. You can also bring one small clutch or fanny pack up to 4.5 x 6.5 in. Empty clear or reusable water bottles are welcome, and you can fill them at any refill station. Every bag is searched and everyone goes through a metal detector at the check-in tent. No glass, coolers, alcohol, or drones, and no bag storage on site.

cards.title: Accessibility
cards.body: The ferries and the event site are wheelchair accessible, and the paths on this part of the island are flat. There is an accessible viewing area at the main stage. Tell us what you need on the registration form.

cards.title: Getting around
cards.body: There are no cars, taxis, or rideshare on the island. The event site is a short walk from both landings. You can bring a bike on the ferry or rent one on the island.

watch.heading: Watch from anywhere
watch.intro: Both days stream live on Twitch and YouTube. Stream times below are in your time zone, with Eastern Time alongside. Add a stream to your calendar so you don't miss the start.

channels.name: Qualifier stream
channels.detail: Commentary on every heat, plus the bracket reveal at {{t:2026-10-17T16:00:00-04:00}}.

channels.name: Finals stream
channels.detail: Team draft, all finals rounds, the creators exhibition match, and the closing ceremony.

channels.name: Replays

watch.vote: Stream chat votes on the Chat Decides route during the grand final, alongside the crowd on the island.

registration.heading: Register
registration.intro: Two ways in. Compete to play a Day 1 qualifier heat, with Day 2 entry included. Spectate to watch either day or both.
registration.demoNotice: Demo form. Nothing is sent anywhere and no emails go out. Your registration is saved only in this browser (localStorage).

types.label: Compete
types.desc: Play one qualifier heat of four games on Day 1. Top three in each heat play the finals on Day 2. Includes Day 2 entry. Ages 18 and up.

types.label: Spectate
types.desc: Watch the heats, the finals, or both from the Parade Ground. All ages. Includes a $5 food truck voucher, so it pays for itself.

items.q: Do I need to be good at games to compete?
items.a: No. The games are simple and short, and most people have never played them in a competition before. Nobody gets to practice ahead of time.

items.q: How do I get to Day 2?
items.a: Finish in the top three of your heat. That gives 18 qualifiers in total. They are announced at the Day 1 bracket reveal, {{t:2026-10-17T16:00:00-04:00}}. On Day 2 you need to be back at check-in by {{t:2026-10-18T10:15:00-04:00}}.

items.q: Can I choose my heat time?
items.a: Yes. You pick one of the six heats when you register, and each heat has 50 spots. You can switch to another heat later with the change my registration link, as long as that heat still has room.

items.q: What if I'm late, or my heat is full?
items.a: Check in at least 30 minutes before your heat. After that, your spot goes to the standby line at the check-in tent, first come, first served. Anyone with a spectator ticket can join standby. If a spot opens, you pay the $25 difference and play.
Light rain, we keep playing. Lightning or strong wind, we pause and post updates on this page and by text. If a day is cancelled, every ticket for that day is refunded in full.

items.q: Can I get a refund if I can't make it?
items.a: Yes, a full refund until Friday 2 October. From Saturday 3 October, two weeks before the event, tickets are non-refundable. You can still switch to a different heat with the change my registration link while that heat has room.

items.q: Is the ferry included in my ticket?
items.a: No. Ferries are free before {{t:2026-10-17T11:00:00-04:00}} on Saturdays and Sundays. After that you buy a round-trip ticket from the ferry operator. Current fares are on govisland.com.

items.q: What if I miss the last ferry?
items.a: There is no other way off the island. Last ferries leave at {{t:2026-10-17T18:00:00-04:00}}, and both days end well before then, so plan to head to your landing by {{t:2026-10-17T17:30:00-04:00}} at the latest.

items.q: Can I bring friends who aren't competing?
items.a: Yes. Spectator tickets are $5, open to all ages, and come with a $5 food truck voucher. Competitors have to be 18 or older.

items.q: Will I be on the stream?
items.a: If you compete, yes. Every heat and every finals round is filmed and streamed. Spectators may also appear in crowd shots. Registering as a competitor means you agree to be filmed.
